subject: System Design
title: The Fallacies of Distributed Computing
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Fallacies of Distributed Computing usable.

hook.text: The network is reliable. Latency is zero. Bandwidth is infinite. All false — but developers assume them daily.

buildup.text: Peter Deutsch defined 8 fallacies that developers wrongly assume when building distributed systems.

discovery.text: Networks fail, latency varies, bandwidth costs money, and the network is not secure. Every assumption breaks.

twist.text: Even experienced teams fall for these fallacies. They only surface under real production load.

climax.text: Understanding these fallacies is the first step to building systems that survive real-world conditions.

punchline.text: Every network assumption you make will eventually break.

quiz.question: Which is one of the 8 fallacies of distributed computing?
